requirement: Agents SHOULD NOT anchor a file under {cite}`requirements.references.anchors` when a more precise reference is available, such as a reference attached to the Rust item that implements or tests the definition. Habeas's bundled agent skills MUST give this direction.
rationale:
**Obligations.** `requirements.references.anchors.guidance` has two clauses.
- Agents SHOULD NOT anchor a file when a more precise reference is available. This is a behavioral norm for agents, and the bundled skills are the only way the product can enforce it. The MUST clause is what carries it.
- Habeas's bundled agent skills MUST give this direction. The skill text must tell agents not to anchor a file whose items can carry a reference themselves.

**Test mapping.** `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[bundled_skills_limit_anchors_to_files_whose_items_cannot_carry_references]` is marked `{test}` for the subject.
- It loads the bundled `habeas` skill's `references/syntax-details.md` through `skill_file`, which uses `include_str!` on the shipped asset.
- It extracts the `## Anchors` section with `section`.
- Through `assert_text`, it asserts that the section contains two phrases:
  - "When a file that implements or tests a requirement cannot carry a reference". This is the positive condition under which anchoring is allowed.
  - "Don't anchor a file whose items can carry a reference themselves". This is the prohibition and the direction the requirement demands.
- `assert_text` panics if either phrase is missing, so the assertions are real.

I read the asset section `assets/skills/habeas/references/syntax-details.md#section[Syntax details]/section[Anchors]`. It contains both phrases, so the test matches the shipped text.

**Remaining questions.**
- The requirement says "skills" in the plural, but the other bundled skills (`habeas-refactor`, `habeas-requirements`) only mention anchors in passing. They don't author declarations, and the requirement doesn't say which skill must carry the direction. The `habeas` skill's syntax reference is the natural home, and the test covers it.
- The skill's wording is slightly more general than "such as a reference attached to the Rust item". The requirement's "such as" is only illustrative, so this is not a gap.

The SHOULD NOT clause is agent behavior and can't be tested directly. The MUST clause is the testable obligation, and it is covered with an adequate assertion. I found no gap.

text: :::{req} anchors.guidance

Agents SHOULD NOT anchor a file under {cite}`requirements.references.anchors` when a more precise reference is available, such as a reference attached to the Rust item that implements or tests the definition. Habeas's bundled agent skills MUST give this direction.
:::{req} anchors
A `{req}` declaration MAY list `:impl:` and `:test:` options, and an `{example}`
declaration MAY list `:test:` options, immediately after its opening fence and
before its body, one per option line, naming a project file path or
`path#selector` for one outline node under
{cite}`requirements.references.outline_selectors`. Each anchor MUST be an `{impl}` or `{test}` edge, under
{cite}`requirements.references.roles`, from the definition to the anchored file or
node, for files that cannot or should not carry a reference themselves.
Paths MUST follow the path rules in {cite}`requirements.ci.schema`. Option lines
MUST NOT form part of the definition's text for evidence comparison or for
requirements inputs, and MUST NOT render as body text.
For each `:test:` anchor, the harness MUST include the selected file or node's
source text in the initial model request under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs` and MUST record that selection
as an evidence input under {cite}`requirements.references.evidence_coverage`,
so changing that source makes the evidence stale.
A `:impl:` anchor alone MUST NOT require an input selecting its source. A path or selector that
does not resolve to a readable, permitted file or node MUST be a validation error naming the
definition and the path; authoring MUST report it before inference. Any other option line in a `{req}` or
`{example}` declaration MUST be a validation error.
